newsitem.title: USA: No wheat export impact from new karnal bunt - USDA.
newsitem.headline: No wheat export impact from new karnal bunt - USDA.

text.p: The latest discovery of the karnal bunt fungus in U.S. wheat should have little or no impact on exports, a senior advisor to Agruclture Secretary Dan Glickman said Thursday.
"The grain in which we've found karnal bunt will be controlled and not exported," trade advisor Paul Drazek said in an interview. "It should not have any appreciable effect at all."

Because many countries refuse to accept wheat that might be contaminated with the fungus, the United States devoted effort earlier this year, following an initial discovery of the fungus, to persuading customers to buy wheat from areas free of karnal bunt.
"Our (export-market) countries continue to accept our wheat on a regionalized basis," Drazek said.

"We will continue to provide additional declarations to countries that wheat they are accepting is coming from regions where karnal bunt is not known to occur. I do not anticipate any appreciable concern in the future."
Drazek also said the USDA karnal-bunt eradication program ultimately would be successful.
"It's not at all that surprisng that we would fnd some spores outsde the original quarantine area," he said.
"Our feeling now is the quarantine is still operative and will be successful."
